title: Rahul Gandhi demands justice for woman killed at Uttarakhand resort
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has met the family of Ankita Bhandari, who was killed at a resort in Uttarakhand for allegedly “resisting the demands of a VIP guest”.

In a social media statement on Saturday (August 15, 2026), Mr. Gandhi said four years had passed since the murder, but even today the family is waiting for justice.

Mr. Gandhi said he met Ms. Bhandari’s parents two days ago. Maintaining that the post-mortem report also confirmed evidence of violence and drowning, he said Ankita’s room at the resort was demolished before any kind of investigation could take place, which was suspicious in itself.

अंकिता भंडारी के परिवार से 2 दिन पहले मिला। चार साल बीत चुके हैं, लेकिन आज भी वो न्याय का इंतज़ार कर रहे हैं - अपनी बच्ची के ख़िलाफ़ एक ऐसे अपराध के लिए जिसकी कोई माफी नहीं।

सिर्फ 19 साल की अंकिता वनंतरा रिज़ॉर्ट में रिसेप्शनिस्ट थीं जहां एक "VIP" मेहमान की शर्मनाक मांग का विरोध… pic.twitter.com/qYN1gIKbmI

— Rahul Gandhi (@RahulGandhi) August 15, 2026

“The most shameful aspect of this tragic case is that the State government itself continues to protect that ‘VIP’ to this day. Why? Because he is a prominent leader of the BJP-RSS. This is the BJP’s warped mentality — protecting rapists and criminals, providing them political cover, even welcoming convicted rapists with garlands. The most repulsive people in the world are those who defend rapists, and the BJP is full of such individuals,” Mr. Gandhi said.

He added the country cannot move forward until this inhuman mentality that treats women as objects is eradicated. “India will move forward only when India’s women move forward—with respect, safety, equality, and justice,” he said.

title: BCI chairman apologises to law students amid enrolment ban controversy
author: Ishita Mishra
content_html:
Days after the Bar Council of India (BCI) tried to prevent NALSAR students from enrolling with State Bar Councils before a backlash forced it to recant, BCI chairman Manan Kumar Mishra on Saturday (August 15, 2026) apologised to law students for any hurt caused by his words or communications.

In a three-page letter issued on Independence Day, Mr. Mishra — who is also a senior advocate and BJP MP — said he regretted and apologised for any of his statements or directives that may have hurt students.

“If anything connected with the present controversy, any of my words, or letter, has hurt the feelings of our law students, I sincerely regret and apologise for the same. There should be no hesitation in saying so. An expression of regret is not a matter of prestige or ego. It is simply an acknowledgment that the feelings and concerns of our students matter,” he said.

Freedom of expression

The BCI chairman did not name any particular institution or directly identify the controversy in his letter. Instead, he focused on the concerns raised by students and stressed that their views should be heard with patience, sensitivity, and respect.

He emphasised that law students, particularly those studying at national law universities and other leading institutions, are capable of forming their own views and should not be subjected to pressure or influence. He said students should be allowed to independently assess the facts and reach their own conclusions.

Acknowledging that protests are an important part of democracy, Mr. Mishra said that students must always remain free to express their views.

‘Keep an open mind’

“At the same time, the legal tradition teaches us something equally important, namely that when further facts or clarifications emerge, every issue should be reconsidered objectively and with an open mind. There is no inconsistency between expressing a genuine grievance and thereafter fairly considering a clarification,” he added.

Describing convocation ceremonies as important milestones in the lives of graduating students and their families, Mr. Mishra said the choice of whether to attend must rest entirely with the students, adding that no student should be forced either to participate or to stay away.

The latest controversy was triggered by NALSAR students who did not want the Chief Justice of India to be the chief guest at the convocation because of his comments about student protests. The BCI had then sought to penalise students for their “campaign” against the CJI, who later slammed the BCI’s actions as well.

Seeking dialogue and mutual respect

The BCI chairman emphasised that differences between the judiciary, the Bar, universities, and law students should not be allowed to damage their relationship in the long term. Disagreements should ultimately be addressed through dialogue, clarification, and mutual respect, he said.

Mr. Mishra appealed for the issue to be approached with an attitude of fairness and reconciliation. “The issue should not be allowed to acquire a political or extraneous colour through outside influence. Our law students are mature and discerning enough to examine the facts, consider the clarification offered, and take their own independent decision,” he added.

title: PM Modi's I-Day speech will be a milestone towards Viksit Bharat journey: Amit Shah
author: PTI
content_html:
Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Saturday (August 15, 2026) said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Independence Day address was imbued with the resolve for Swadeshi and prosperity and added that it will prove to be a milestone in the journey towards becoming a leading nation across all sectors.

In a post on X, Mr. Shah said Mr. Modi outlined a comprehensive roadmap to build a ‘Viksit Bharat’ driven by the spirit of ‘nation first’, ‘drug-free’ and a ‘safe India’.

He also said the Prime Minister highlighted the unprecedented progress made over the last 12 years in sectors such as semiconductors, critical minerals, energy, and railway transport.

He presented the mantra of Saptadhara — seven pillars of strength — to propel the country to new heights and achieve self-reliance across all sectors, Mr. Shah said.

“To channel the potential of the youth, Modi Ji announced initiatives to provide AI skilling to over one crore young people in a single year, establish a network for free online coaching, and launch a talent hunt campaign for the 2036 Olympics,” Mr. Shah said on ‘X’.

Ambitious targets

The Prime Minister set ambitious targets, such as achieving 100 gigawatts of nuclear power capacity and establishing eight new semiconductor units by 2047, he said.

In another post, Mr. Shah said the spirited rallying cry of the freedom movement — Vande Mataram — was sung from the ramparts of the Red Fort for the first time today, 80 years after Independence.

“Witnessing this historic moment not only gave me goosebumps but filled my entire being with sheer ecstasy,” he said.

title: Ramdev expresses concern over growing youth unrest on education, recruitment issues
author: Ishita Mishra
content_html:
Yoga guru Baba Ramdev on Independence Day warned that growing irregularities in education and government recruitment could trigger stronger youth protests across the country, urging authorities to address the concerns before the situation escalates.

Speaking to reporters after hoisting the national flag at Patanjali Yogpeeth in Uttarakhand’s Haridwar on Saturday (August 15, 2026), Mr. Ramdev said, “I am seeing protests by students everyday over unavailability of teachers in schools or sometimes of books and proper education. Even basic facilities such as electricity, drinking water and toilets remained unavailable in some places.”

He further alleged that question papers get leaked in competitive examinations and that the marks secured by students in board examinations have become useless.

Rampant corruption

Turning to government recruitment, the yoga practitioner claimed that corruption was particularly rampant during interview-based selections.

“They choose people from their own caste, community, organisation and ideology....despite this, lakhs are being asked as bribe,” he said adding that such acts are not just against democracy but also justice.

Warning that failure to address such concerns could lead to larger protests, Mr. Ramdev called on authorities to “mend their ways” and undertake reforms in the education and recruitment systems.

Need for course correction

Stating that there is still time to correct the system, Mr. Ramdev asked the government to correct itself.

“Sudhar jao....desh me ghapla bahut hai...ye theek kar lo (Mend your ways…there is a lot of corruption and irregularities in the country. Fix these problems),” he said adding that continued inaction could result in stronger protests across the country.

At the same time, he cautioned against violence and disorder during demonstrations. While acknowledging the right of young people to raise grievances, he said protests should remain peaceful and disciplined.

Mr. Ramdev also criticised the increasingly hostile relationship between the government and the Opposition, saying political and caste-based divisions were damaging democratic discourse. He urged both sides to show greater respect and restraint.

title: Bishnoi comes out in support of Rao Inderjit, says ignoring seniors will weaken BJP
author: Ashok Kumar
content_html:
A day after Union Minister of State for Planning and BJP’s Gurugram MP Rao Inderjit Singh publicly questioned the manner in which the party’s Partition Day programme was organised, senior party leader and former MP Kuldeep Bishnoi on Saturday came out in his support, stressing that the experience of senior leaders must be respected while creating opportunities for the younger generation.

Mr. Singh, speaking at the BJP programme commemorating the horrors of Partition in Gurugram on Friday, had expressed displeasure over the exclusion of local leaders from the event and said he objected to the fact that people from different areas had been invited while local representatives had not.

Mr. Bishnoi subsequently took to “X” to back Mr. Singh, underlining the importance of respecting senior leaders who have spent decades building the party and maintaining a public connect.

“The decades of political experience of senior leaders is the party’s invaluable asset,” Mr. Bishnoi said, adding that such leaders had witnessed political ups and downs, managed the organisation during difficult periods and earned their position through years of work among the people.

He cautioned that ignoring senior leaders or sending any message that they were not being accorded due respect could weaken the organisation rather than strengthen it.

Referring specifically to Mr. Singh, Mr. Bishnoi said the Union Minister had a “very significant stature” in Haryana politics and enjoyed a broad public base and respect. He added that he personally held him in high regard and admired his political experience, struggles and contribution to the State.

“The BJP is a strong organisation, and its strength lies in better coordination between the experience of senior leadership and the energy of young leadership. Respect for seniors and opportunities for the new generation -- both must go hand in hand,” said Mr. Bishnoi, son of late Chief Minister Bhajan Lal.

Mr. Bishnoi’s intervention comes against the backdrop of earlier tensions within the Haryana BJP over remarks concerning his family. A few months ago, BJP Rajya Sabha MP Rekha Sharma had triggered controversy by alleging at a public rally that former Chief Minister Bhajan Lal and his son Chander Mohan had won elections through “badmashi” (malpractice).

The remarks sparked a political row, following which Mr. Bishnoi had cautioned the BJP leadership against arrogance and disrespect towards senior leaders.

title: Yakshagana, Dhol Tasha, Garba add colour to Bengaluru’s first Freedom Habba
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
For the first time, Bengaluru celebrated Independence Day by hosting Freedom Habba in front of the grand steps of Vidhana Soudha on Saturday. Organised by the Karnataka government the event was a first-of-a-kind, citizen-led festival.

There were people from diverse communities, States and districts who were dressed in traditional attire to showcase their folk traditions, culture, music and dance. From Karnataka’s Yakshagana, Veeragaase to Hulivesha, Maharashtra’s dhol tasha, Gujarati Garba , to West Bengal’s Dhanuchi Naach, Sikh traditional martial arts including Chakkar bazi and Gatka, various forms of art were exhibited.

Atleast 30 such teams paraded their art and skills for nearly half a kilometer. At the end of the parade, each team went on the stage set at the entrance of Vidhana Soudha and explained the importance of their art, culture and traditions.

Amit J, a degree student from Government Arts College in Bengaluru who was at the celebrations, said, “Our team is called Kalamilana. When we got a call from the representatives of the government, we were happy to participate and showcase Yakshagana. .”

Meanwhile, Kuntur Kumara team had travelled from Malavalli in Mandya district to perform Puje Kunitha. Explaining the art form, he said, “Dancers balance heavy, decorated structures with colourful silk cloth and flowers on their heads and do acrobatic movements. Puje Kunitha is performed during grama devathe’s worship or festival in villages. It is mostly performed in Mandya district, Mysuru, Ramanagara and Channapattana.”

Besides the parade, an immersive living museum called India’s Freedom Trail showcased information on Salt Satyagraha, Quit India Movement, while district themed pavilions showcased contributions of Sangolli Rayanna, Rani Chennamma to highlight Karnataka’s contribution to India’s freedom struggle. There were also a Constitution square, children’s games and activity zones.

Vaishnavi R, a visitor at the Freedom Habba, said, “I had never seen Vidhana Soudha so close. I had booked a guided tour in which all the important spots inside Soudha, a replica of Vidhana Soudha made of sandalwood, wood carvings and the meaning behind it were explained. Later, I walked out to be part of the Freedom Habba. Being a Bengalurean, I am celebrating Independence day in a unique way.”

Confusion among metro commuters, park visitors

As the Cubbon Park started closing at 6 p.m., visitors to the park were left confused about the exit route from the park. While they tried to exit from roads close to High Court and B R Ambedkar Metro Station, police personnel directed them towards other alternative routes like BSNL Gate, Bal Bhavan Gate and the gate near Century club.

Police personnel ensured that only those with registered QR codes were going for the habba and allowed entry near GPO office, BSNL gate and MS building.

The screening process created bottlenecks for people not attending the festival. In one instance, an elderly man was stopped by the police despite repeatedly explaining that he was merely heading to Shivajinagar and not the event. Finally, he was allowed to exit.

Meanwhile, Namma metro services were stopped at Cubbon Park, Sir M Visvesvaraya Metro stations and Vidhana Soudha metro stations for sometime and commuters were allowed to get down at MG Road and Nadaprabhu Kempegowda Metro Stations until 9.30 p.m. Services resumed once the programme ended.

title: Independence Day celebrations held in Vellore, nearby districts
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
The 80th Independence Day was celebrated with fervour in Vellore, Ranipet, Tirupattur, and Tiruvannamalai districts on Saturday.

In Vellore, Collector P.S. Leela Alex unfurled the tricolour and reviewed the Guard of Honour at Nethaji Stadium. She honoured 66 freedom fighters’ family members in recognition of their contributions. She also distributed appreciation certificates to 241 government staff for good work. Earlier, the Collector hoisted the tricolour on the ramparts of Vellore Fort and paid floral tributes at the Mahatma Gandhi statue at the entrance of the campus.

title: BSNL to expand 4G coverage, FTTH services in Dharwad-Davangere circle
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL) will expand its 4G network and strengthen broadband connectivity across rural and urban areas of the Dharwad Telecom Circle, Senior General Manager Dhananjaykumar Tripathi said on Saturday.

Addressing a press conference in Hubballi on Saturday, Mr. Tripathi said BSNL had installed around 65 new 4G saturation towers in the Hubballi Business Area (BA) during 2025-26. Another 422 base transceiver stations (BTS) had been installed under Phase 9.2 to improve data speed and network capacity.

“During 2026-27, BSNL plans to install 14 additional saturation sites and survey 47 villages for the 4G saturation project. Another 123 BTS units are planned, including 20 to improve coverage in underserved areas. The company has set a target of 40,000 new gross mobile connections during the year,” he said.

Special offers

Mr. Tripathi said BSNL was offering free all-India roaming to mobile subscribers. As part of its Independence Day promotions, new and mobile number portability (MNP) port-in customers can obtain SIM cards for ₹1 and ₹51 under separate schemes.

“The ₹1 scheme offers 1 GB of data a day, 100 SMS messages and unlimited voice calls for 24 days, while the ₹51 scheme provides 2 GB of daily data, 100 SMS messages and unlimited calls for 28 days. BSNL has also introduced monthly voice and data vouchers priced at ₹107, ₹147 and ₹153. An Independence Day offer on the ₹2,399 plan provides 412 days of validity, unlimited voice calls, 2 GB of data a day and 100 SMS messages,” he said.

FTTH expansion

Mr. Tripathi said BSNL had 20,844 working Fibre-to-the-Home (FTTH) connections at the end of 2025-26 and had added 5,543 gross connections during the year. All exchanges in the Hubballi BA had been migrated to Next Generation Network technology. For 2026-27, BSNL’s target is 14,000 new FTTH connections.

The company is offering free Wi-Fi modems/ONTs to rural and urban broadband customers with warranty support for two to two and a half years. Installation charges for new FTTH connections have also been waived until September 30, 2026.

Deputy General Managers Rajkumar Asangi and R.S. Kadam briefed on the initiatives taken to improve BSNL services, including setting up exclusive teams to immediately attend to technical issues. Mr. Asangi said that the toll-free number 1800-4444 and WhatsApp service would enable customers to book connections and register complaints. BSNL would also provide doorstep assistance for new landline and broadband connections.
